battle.name: 辛未洋擾
battle.brief: 一八七一年六月，美國亞洲艦隊藉謝爾曼號事件索賠與通商要求進入江華海峽，遭江華砲台射擊，隨即以艦砲壓制、登陸草芝鎭，攻德津鎭與廣城堡。卡面這門線膛野砲代表同期歐洲陸軍剛換裝的世代：線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠，砲兵第一次能在射程上贏步兵，廣城堡守軍用的仍是只發實心鐵球的舊式前裝砲。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方是美國與朝鮮，兩邊的軍事架構幾乎沒有交集。美國一方派出亞洲艦隊，即當時部署在西太平洋的遠東分遣隊：旗艦科羅拉多號（Colorado）連同阿拉斯加號（Alaska）、莫諾加希拉號（Monongahela）、貝尼西亞號（Benicia）與砲艦帕洛斯號（Palos）共五艘，合計攜帶八十五門砲、一千二百三十名艦上人員與海軍陸戰隊員，指揮權在亞洲艦隊司令羅傑斯（John Rodgers）少將手中，外交授權則來自駐清公使 F. F. Low，艦隊的任務寫得很直白：若朝鮮拒絕談判，就用武力逼它簽約。朝鮮一方是李氏朝鮮高宗朝廷，攝政的興宣大院君主持朝政，軍權分成兩套系統：一是江華島沿岸各鎭堡的守備，由鎭撫中軍與各營哨將分領；二是三道水軍，由統制使魚在淵率領五哨戰船駐泊漢江與京畿海面，負責封住海峽的出入。守備靠的是朝廷撥發的舊式火器與固定砲位，缺的是能隨命令機動的火力；美軍那一側則有軍艦、登陸部隊，以及隨行的工程、醫務、攝影人員。清朝並未參戰，但謝爾曼號事件的善後始終牽涉清廷的處分，這是雙方交涉背後的外部壓力。
countriesEn: The two sides were the United States and the Joseon court, and their military structures had almost nothing in common. The American force was the Asiatic Squadron, the United States Navy's far-western detachment in the Pacific: the flagship Colorado, together with Alaska, Monongahela, Benicia and the gunboat Palos, five ships in all, carrying eighty-five guns and one thousand two hundred and thirty officers and men, including marines, under the command of Asiatic Squadron commander Rear Admiral John Rodgers, with the diplomatic authority for the whole business resting with the United States minister to China, F. F. Low. The squadron's instructions were blunt: if Korea refused to negotiate, force the treaty by arms. On the Korean side stood the court of the Joseon dynasty under King Gojong, with the regent Heungseon Daewongun directing the government. Military authority was split into two systems. The first was the garrison of the island forts along the coast of Ganghwa, held by the Jinmu Junggun and the commanders of the various posts and pickets. The second was the Samdo naval force, five squadrons of war boats under the overall command of the fleet admiral Yu Jae-yeon, stationed in the Han River and the waters around the capital to seal the approaches to the strait. The defence rested on old state-issued small arms and on guns fixed in place; what it lacked was firepower that could move on command. The Americans, by contrast, brought warships, a landing force, and engineers, medical staff and a photographic team. Qing China did not take part, but the aftermath of the General Sherman affair always implicated the Qing court's own handling of the case, and that was the external pressure sitting behind the negotiations on both sides.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊，各自的決定都很硬。美國方面，亞洲艦隊司令羅傑斯是全盤計畫的執行者：不僅決定派兩艘軍艦進入江華海峽「測量」，也在朝鮮拒絕道歉與賠償之後，定下十天內登陸報復的最後通牒；此役是他率領的亞洲艦隊第一次實戰，他日後升任海軍上將，一八七四年又指揮北太平洋分艦隊。駐清公使 F. F. Low 持有政府的全權授權，遠征一旦成功，通商條約的框架也隨之而來。朝鮮方面，攝政的興宣大院君（一八二〇至一八九八）是真正作主的人：他不接受美方的任何條件，屢次要求艦隊退出江華海峽，還在京城鍾路與全國各地豎立斥和碑，把拒絕通商寫成石頭上的政策。水軍統制使魚在淵是廣城堡一線的實際指揮，他率五哨戰船在海峽內游弋，又在六百餘名守軍之間周旋，最後死在廣城堡，出生年份不詳，只留下年數十歲的壽命與一面被奪走的帥字旗。那面旗被美軍帶回美國，直到二〇〇七年才隨兩國交流歸還朝鮮，成為這場戰爭最耐人尋味的物證。回看遠因，一八六六年平壤大同江的謝爾曼號事件中殉難的朝鮮將校，後來有六十三人被清廷處死，廣城堡內至今立有順節祠紀念他們，那座祠正是此役爭奪的城牆之內。
peopleEn: The decisive figures fall on either side, and both sets of them were stubborn. On the American side Rear Admiral John Rodgers, commander of the Asiatic Squadron, carried out the entire plan: he decided to send two warships into the Ganghwa Strait to make a survey, and after Korea refused to apologise or pay, he set a ten-day ultimatum warning that a landing would follow. The engagement was the first combat of the squadron he commanded; he was later promoted to admiral and in 1874 took charge of the North Pacific Squadron. The minister to China, F. F. Low, held the full authority of the government, and with the expedition's success a framework for a commercial treaty would have followed. On the Korean side the regent Heungseon Daewongun (1820-1898) was the man in charge. He accepted none of the American terms, demanded again and again that the squadron withdraw from the Ganghwa Strait, and had rejection-of-intercourse stones erected in the Jongno district of the capital and in districts all over the country, turning a policy of refusing contact into a sentence carved in stone. Yu Jae-yeon, the fleet admiral of the Samdo naval force, commanded the actual defence of Gwangseong Castle. He led the five squadrons of war boats in the strait and moved among the six hundred or so men of the garrison, and he died at the castle; his year of birth is not recorded, and he left behind only a life measured in a few tens of years and a commander's flag that was taken from him. That flag was carried back to the United States and returned to Korea only in 2007, and it has become the most thought-provoking relic of the whole affair. Further back, of the Korean officers who died in the General Sherman affair of 1866 on the Taedong River near Pyongyang, sixty-three were later executed by the Qing authorities, and the shrine inside Gwangseong Castle still commemorates them, in the very fortifications that this expedition fought over.
kits: 卡面是一門前裝線膛野砲，歐洲在一八五〇年前後換裝的那一型：線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠，砲兵第一次可以在射程上壓過步兵，克里米亞戰爭之後它成為各國陸軍的制式野砲。要說清它在江華島上的位置，就得把這場戰鬥裡實際存在的兩代砲分開來看。第一代是守軍的舊式前裝砲：江華島各堡與砲台沿用明清傳入的銅砲與鐵砲，架在石造堡壘的砲眼裡發射實心鐵球，射界被牆體壓得極窄，轉向緩慢，只能守著固定的角度打；美軍登陸之後，這些砲不是被當場擊毀，就是被推落海峽。第二代是美軍的艦載火砲：五艘軍艦合帶八十五門砲，主力是九吋達格倫滑膛前裝砲，以及七吋與六〇磅帕羅特線膛後膛砲，旗艦一艦即載四十餘門；登陸當日，砲兵隊把隨艦運來的火砲與艦載砲拉上灘頭充作野砲使用，配合工兵隊在正面施壓，砲火把草芝鎭的守軍與砲台打成焦土。個人火器的差距更大：美軍裝備普利茅斯卡賓槍、斯普林菲爾德步槍與雷明登後膛步槍，軍官另帶單發與連發左輪；朝鮮守軍用的仍是火繩槍（朝鮮稱華勝槍），配少量手擲炸藥，船上則是數門小型手砲與火藥船。差距不在於人數，而在於火砲的射程、射速，以及能不能隨意轉向。
kitsEn: The card shows a rifled muzzle-loading field gun, the type European armies exchanged into around 1850: rifling lets the same charge travel further, artillery could for the first time outrange infantry on the range, and after the Crimean War it became the standard field piece of every army. To place it at Ganghwa Island, the two generations of gun actually present in that fight have to be separated. The first is the old muzzle-loading gun of the defenders. The island forts and batteries used bronze and iron pieces inherited from the Ming and Qing period, set in embrasures in the stone works and firing solid iron balls; the walls cut their arcs down to a very narrow sector, they traversed slowly, and they could only engage a fixed angle. After the American landing these guns were either destroyed on the spot or pushed down into the strait. The second generation is the American ship's battery. The five warships carried eighty-five guns between them, the bulk of them nine-inch Dahlgren smoothbores together with seven-inch and sixty-pounder Parrott rifled breech-loaders, the flagship alone carrying more than forty. On the day of the landing the artillery detachment hauled ashore the guns carried in the ships and the ship's own pieces, using them as field guns, with the engineers pushing forward under their fire and reducing the Choji-jin garrison and batteries to a scorched ruin. The gap in small arms was wider still: the Americans were equipped with Plymouth carbines, Springfield rifles and Remington breech-loading rifles, and officers carried single-shot and repeating revolvers; the Korean defenders still used matchlock muskets, called hwaseung rifles, with a little hand-thrown explosive, while the boats carried a few small hand cannon and their powder magazines. The difference lay not in numbers but in range, rate of fire, and the freedom to traverse.
tactics: 美軍的整套動作是教科書式的砲艦外交加兩棲突擊。第一步是不打招呼：六月一日至二日，兩艘軍艦單方面駛入江華海峽做水深測量，等於宣布主權；朝鮮沿岸砲台在孫乭項一帶以奇襲射擊回應，美軍趁勢指控朝鮮野蠻，並開出條件：道歉、賠償、派代表談判，十日內不答就登陸。第二步是登陸，六月十日，十個中隊分成兩面同時上岸，艦砲先把草芝鎭的守軍與砲台打成焦土，工兵隊隨即架設浮橋、拆除灘頭障礙，醫務隊與攝影班跟著上岸，把這一仗變成可以帶回美國的影像。第三步是攻堅，六月十一日先無血佔領德津鎭，再以海陸兩面同時射擊約一小時，攻下廣城堡，奪取守軍的帥字旗，在城頭升起星條旗。整個過程裡，美軍的優勢是火砲可以自由轉向、射程遠、射速快，弱點是登陸兵力有限，攻堅時仍得靠步兵面對城牆。朝鮮的戰法則是一套以守待戰的辦法：砲眼固定、射界狹窄，岸砲搶先奇襲，海上由五哨戰船牽制，廣城堡的六百餘名守軍以鎭撫中軍居中，據城死守，寧可玉石俱焚也不投降，最後以傷亡與陣亡收場。事後朝廷不但拒絕談判，還在海峽入口與京城豎起斥和碑，把整條海峽封成禁區。
tacticsEn: The American method was textbook gunboat diplomacy followed by an amphibious assault. The first step was to act without asking: on 1 and 2 June two warships sailed single-handedly into the Ganghwa Strait to sound the depths, which amounted to an announcement of sovereignty. The coastal batteries answered with a surprise fire at Sondol-mok, and the Americans promptly accused the Koreans of barbarity, then set their terms: an apology, reparations, and an envoy for talks, with the warning that a landing would follow if no answer came in ten days. The second step was the landing. On 10 June ten companies came ashore on two fronts at once; the ship's guns first reduced the Choji-jin garrison and batteries to a scorched ruin, the engineers then laid their pontoons and cleared the beach, and the medical staff and photographic party went up with them, turning the fight into images that could be carried home to America. The third step was the assault on the works. On 11 June Deokjin-jin was occupied without a shot, and then Gwangseong Castle was taken after about an hour of combined fire from sea and land, the garrison's commander's flag was seized, and the Stars and Stripes was raised over the fort. Through all of it the American advantage was artillery that could traverse freely, with long range and a fast rate of fire; the weakness was the small size of the landing force, which still had to put infantry against the walls. The Korean method was a battle of waiting: guns fixed in embrasures with narrow arcs, the shore battery firing first in a surprise, the five squadrons of war boats contesting the water, and the six hundred or so men at Gwangseong Castle holding the line with the Jinmu Junggun at the centre, resolved to die rather than surrender, and the action ending in wounds and death. Afterwards the court not only refused to negotiate but set up rejection-of-intercourse stones at the entrance of the strait and in the capital, sealing the whole channel as a forbidden zone.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。艦隊五艘，合計八十五門砲（朝方史料常記作八十餘門），艦上人員一千二百三十名；其中參加六月十日登陸的陸戰隊員，朝鮮官方史料記為六百四十四人，編為十個中隊，另配砲兵隊、工兵隊、醫務隊與攝影班。守方在廣城堡一線的兵力約六百人，由鎭撫中軍魚在淵率領，另有江華各堡與三道水軍五哨分佈在海峽兩側。時間表清楚：五月初中旬艦隊在長崎集結並操演約半個月，五月十六日出發，五月十九日抵南陽灣，六月一日至二日測量海峽，同日或次日發生孫乭項砲擊事件，美方給十天期限，六月十日登陸草芝鎭，六月十一日攻下德津鎭與廣城堡，六月十二日撤至勿淄島。傷亡數字雙方記載差距很大：美方記錄陣亡三人、受傷十人；美軍另稱朝軍陣亡三百五十人、受傷二十人，朝鮮方面的記錄是陣亡五十七人，高宗實錄的補充記載則為死亡五十三人、受傷二十四人。砲擊持續時間有約一小時的說法。五年前的一八六六年事件、此後兩度流產的遠征計畫、二〇〇七年歸還的帥字旗（一百三十六年後），以及一八七六年的江華島條約與一八八二年的朝美修好條規，都是可以用來核對這場戰爭座標的年份。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The squadron numbered five ships carrying eighty-five guns between them, the Korean records often giving the figure as eighty-odd, with one thousand two hundred and thirty officers and men aboard; the Korean official history puts the marines who landed on 10 June at six hundred and forty-four, organised into ten companies, with an artillery detachment, engineers, medical staff and a photographic party attached. On the defending side about six hundred men were deployed in the Gwangseong Castle sector under the Jinmu Junggun commander Yu Jae-yeon, with the island forts and the five squadrons of the Samdo naval force spread along both sides of the strait. The timetable is clear. Early to mid May the squadron assembled at Nagasaki and spent about half a month in sea manoeuvres; on 16 May it sailed, on 19 May it reached Namyang Bay, and on 1 and 2 June it surveyed the strait. The bombardment at Sondol-mok came on the same day or the day after, the Americans set ten days for an answer, the landing at Choji-jin was made on 10 June, Deokjin-jin and Gwangseong Castle fell on 11 June, and the squadron withdrew to the island of Murechi on 12 June. The casualty figures differ widely between the sides: the Americans recorded three dead and ten wounded; they claimed three hundred and fifty Korean dead and twenty wounded; the Korean figure is fifty-seven dead; and the supplementary record in the Annals of King Gojong gives fifty-three dead and twenty-four wounded. The bombardment is said to have lasted about an hour. The 1866 affair five years earlier, the two expedition plans that had been drawn up and abandoned, the commander's flag returned in 2007, one hundred and thirty-six years after the fighting, and the Ganghwa Treaty of 1876 and the Korean-American Treaty of 1882, are all dates that can be used to check the coordinates of this war.
cause: 起因要從一八六六年說起。那年八月，美國商船謝爾曼號在平壤一帶的大同江上誤入朝鮮水域，遭到朝鮮砲台射擊並被扣留，船上的人員死傷，事件成為美國要求賠償與開港的直接理由；事後朝鮮有六十三名將校在清朝依約處死，這件事遂成了兩國之間長期未解的心結。美國此後多次派船北上探視，並兩度擬定遠征計畫而未實行，到一八七一年才在駐清公使 F. F. Low 手上取得全權，決定以砲艦外交強行開港；同年春天，美方巡檢船在朝鮮近海扣押朝鮮船隻、又被指稱造成傷亡，把摩擦推到臨界點。朝鮮的應對則是一貫的鎖國：朝廷拒絕通商，屢次退回西式要求，海峽入口與京城的斥和碑就是這條路線的物證。真正決定開打的是朝鮮內部的分歧：議政府中有人主張接納美方要求以換取轉圜，攝政的興宣大院君則斷然不允，力主寧可交戰也不開港。於是美軍六月初抵達海峽之際，雙方都已經站在只能開火的立場上，衝突的爆點反而是一場測量航行與一門岸砲之間的擦撞。
causeEn: The story begins in 1866. That August the American merchantman General Sherman entered Korean waters on the Taedong River near Pyongyang by mistake, was fired on by the Korean batteries and was seized, with loss of life among her people; the affair became the direct ground on which the United States demanded reparations and the opening of ports. In the aftermath sixty-three Korean officers were executed by the Qing court under the terms agreed with the Americans, and the affair turned into a long-standing grudge between the two countries. The United States afterwards made repeated voyages north to make contact and twice drew up plans for an expedition without ever carrying them out, and only in 1871 did the expedition become possible, when full authority was placed in the hands of the minister to China, F. F. Low, who resolved to force the ports open by gunboat diplomacy. In the spring of the same year an American revenue vessel seized a Korean ship off the Korean coast and was accused of causing deaths, pushing the friction to its limit. The Korean response was a consistent policy of exclusion: the court refused commerce, turned back Western demands again and again, and the rejection-of-intercourse stones at the entrance of the strait and in the capital are the physical record of that line. What actually set the war off was a disagreement inside Korea. Some in the Council of State argued for accepting the American terms in order to buy room to manoeuvre; the regent Heungseon Daewongun flatly refused, holding that war was preferable to opening the ports. By the time the American squadron reached the strait in early June, therefore, both sides had taken up positions from which only fire remained, and the spark was a survey voyage brushing against a shore gun.
impact: 影響是雙向的，而且延續得比人預期的久。對朝鮮而言，這一仗等於把鎖國政策的最後一道防線換成了石頭：斥和碑自此從京城的鍾路一路立到江華島，德津一帶甚至立碑禁止外國船隻靠近。朝鮮保住了開港紅線，卻也付出廣城堡被毀、守軍折損與主將陣亡的代價，朝廷在廷議上的共識反而更強：既然美軍的砲火與登陸都擋不住，開港只是早晚。事實上五年之後，日本用江華島條約與丙子正使朴泳孝一行做到了美國沒有做到的事，一八七六年開港議定書簽訂，朝鮮的鎖國體制自此崩解；一八八二年，朝鮮又不得不與美國簽下朝美修好條規，太平洋彼岸的壓力終於變成紙面上的義務。對美國而言，這是一次沒有拿到任何通商條約的遠征：亞洲艦隊第一次實戰，卻在沒有迫使朝鮮開港的情況下主動退走，說明單靠幾艘帆船加登陸部隊，還不足以讓一個決心閉關的國家改變主意；此後美國轉向更貼近的經濟手段，而這套以艦隊為後盾的包含外交路線，後來被日本在同一片海域接著走了一遍。歷史記憶則落在人身上：魚在淵陣亡、帥字旗被奪並在美國保存了一百三十六年，順節祠與無名戰歿碑留在廣城堡，二〇〇七年旗幟歸還，成為韓美之間少數被正面處理的舊物。
impactEn: The consequences ran in both directions and lasted longer than anyone expected. For Korea the fight meant replacing the last physical line of the policy of exclusion with stone: the rejection-of-intercourse steles now ran from the Jongno district of the capital down to Ganghwa Island, and at Deokjin there was even a stone put up to keep foreign vessels away. Korea held the line against opening its ports, but it paid for that in the destruction of Gwangseong Castle, in losses among the garrison and in the death of the commander; and the consensus inside the Council of State grew stronger rather than weaker, since if the American guns and landing parties could not be held off, opening was only a matter of time. In fact, five years later Japan achieved what the United States had not: the Ganghwa Treaty and the mission of Pak Yeong-hyo as minister in 1876 brought the ports open and the structure of exclusion collapsed. In 1882 Korea had to sign a treaty of amity with the United States, and the pressure from across the Pacific finally became an obligation on paper. For the Americans this was an expedition that brought home no commercial treaty: the first combat of the Asiatic Squadron ended with a voluntary withdrawal without the ports being opened, showing that a few sailing ships and a landing force were not yet enough to change the mind of a country determined on shutting itself in. The United States afterwards turned to more immediate economic instruments, and the line of gunboat diplomacy backed by a squadron was later walked over the same waters by Japan. The historical memory settled on people: the death of Yu Jae-yeon, the seizure of his commander's flag and its one hundred and thirty-six years in America, the shrine and the monument to the unnamed dead left at Gwangseong Castle, and the return of the flag in 2007, one of the few objects from the old quarrel that the two countries have dealt with face to face.
result: 結果是雙方各得其所，也各自留下疤。美軍在戰術上做得很漂亮：草芝鎭被艦砲打成焦土，德津鎭無血佔領，廣城堡在海陸兩面射擊下一小時後陷落，守軍的帥字旗被奪走，美國國旗曾在城頭升起。戰略上卻一無所獲：沒有條約，沒有賠款，沒有開港；六月十二日全艦退回勿淄島，隨後返回日本，遠征宣告終止。朝鮮這一邊守住的是開港這條底線，輸掉的是廣城堡與數百名守軍，魚在淵戰死之後，朝廷把這場戰爭記作辛未洋擾，把洋擾寫進國家的正式敘述裡，成為日後反覆被引用的抵抗記憶；美方則把它叫作朝鮮遠征或一八七一年的朝美之戰，並把旗幟帶回國。從兵器史的角度看，這一仗也是滑膛前裝砲的最後幾場大規模對決之一：固定砲眼上的舊砲抵擋不住可自由轉向的艦砲與上岸的野砲，正是卡面那門線膛野砲所代表的射程革命在遠東的餘波；而它真正留下的功課，是後來在技術上更進一步的艦砲與後膛線膛砲，終於在一八七六年的江華島把朝鮮的砲台一一清除。
resultEn: The result was that each side got something and each was left with a scar. The Americans did the tactical part well: Choji-jin was reduced to a scorched ruin by the ship's guns, Deokjin-jin was occupied without a shot, Gwangseong Castle fell after an hour of fire from sea and land, the garrison's commander's flag was taken, and the American flag was raised over the fort. Strategically they got nothing: no treaty, no reparations, no open ports. On 12 June the squadron withdrew to the island of Murechi and then went back to Japan, and the expedition was over. On the Korean side the bottom line that mattered was kept, that the ports should not open, but the price was Gwangseong Castle and several hundred of the garrison; after the death of Yu Jae-yeon the court recorded the war as the Shinmi Western Disturbance, wrote the word disturbance into the state's own official narrative, and turned it into a memory of resistance that has been quoted again and again since. The Americans called it the Korean Expedition, or the Korean-American War of 1871, and took the flag home with them. From the point of view of the history of weapons, this was one of the last large-scale confrontations between smoothbore muzzle-loading guns: the old pieces in fixed embrasures could not hold against ship guns that traversed freely and field guns brought ashore, which is precisely the reverberation in the Far East of the range revolution represented by the rifled muzzle-loading field gun on this card. The real lesson it left was that the technically superior ship guns and rifled breech-loaders would, at Ganghwa in 1876, clear the Korean batteries away one by one.
